descriptions.2802133:
Thuishaven is not a club, or a warehouse. It’s a unique experience. Located on the Western outskirts of Amsterdam, the site is surrounded by heavy industry, massive oil tankers and scrap metal yards. Thuishaven has several stages, bars, surreal decoration pieces and curiosities. Incorporating materials purchased or found at neighboring scrap yards, the site radiates a raw and industrial atmosphere. During the winter set-up (October - April), all stages are housed indoor, in heated tents and a newly crafted hangar. The summer set-up (May - September) hosts a mesmerizing open air stage plus the option to use both tent and hangar for a raveyer vibe. With a track record of 200 festivals and counting, the site is ever evolving. Every new visit brings to light new details and new surprises—making it one of Amsterdam’s most extraordinary venues.

German DJ and producer Klangkuenstler is one of the defining voices of the modern techno scene. He stands for an uncompromising sound – a powerful blend of old-school and new-school Techno. With his brand “Outworld,” Klangkuenstler brings his bold vision of Techno to life, not just as a label but also as an event series with an innovative production concept. Blending futuristic aesthetics with raw, industrial sound, Outworld transports the crowd into a dystopian, sci-fi-inspired world.

ÄSTHETICS is an electronic music project developed by a Mexican artist collective based in Barcelona. ADE 2026 marks our third consecutive year organizing official events during Amsterdam Dance Event.

Our mission is to create a platform connecting artists, audiences and electronic music communities across Mexico, Barcelona and Europe. Across these three years, our ADE projects have provided a platform for approximately 30-40 DJs and artists, bringing together Mexican, Barcelona-based and European talent who actively contribute to their respective local electronic music scenes.

Our purpose goes beyond producing a party during ADE: we use Amsterdam as a meeting point where artists can perform,exchange ideas, build professional relationships and experience one of the world's most important electronic music gatherings as active participants.

Long before melodic techno became a formula, Kevin Rodrigues was approaching electronic music like a composer rather than a DJ. Continuing the marathon on October 24 at De Fik for a full day in the garden. From 12:00 until 22:00, expect a curated soundtrack spanning the deeper and more driving corners of techno, set against one of Amsterdam's most unique outdoor spaces. A chance to slow things down without losing momentum, bringing the community together in the daylight before another long night ahead. Good music, good people, and ten hours under the open sky.

De Fik Garden, built by and for the community, is a raw, ever-evolving space where artists, collectives, and creatives come together to shape their own stages. As you approach Deep Seeing Currents by Olafur Eliasson, you are slowly enveloped by darkness and the sounds of life underwater. Layers of oceanic cacophony – whale songs, rumbling of hydrothermal vents, and human-made noises, among others – surround you, while the vibrations can be felt throughout your entire body, emulating the experience of pressure in the deep sea. Above and around you, lights flash and seem to descend like the hypnotic circulation of marine snow, the organic and inorganic particles essential to life in the deep sea. The immersive sound of Deep seeing currents is brought to life by 4DSOUND. The exhibition is located inside the ARTIS Aquarium and can be visited with a valid ARTIS Park ticket. Tickets are available through the ARTIS website.

descriptions.2814580: Originally from Tokyo, Japan, Takuya Nakamura moved to the United States in 1990 to study under the legendary jazz theorist and composer George Russell at the New England Conservatory of Music. Under Russell’s tutelage, Nakamura honed his craft and developed a profound understanding of jazz theory and composition, which would become fundamental to his innovative approach to music. In 94′ Nakamura moved to New York City, where he quickly became a staple in the vibrant Jazz and Jungle scene. He has worked with legendary figures such as Quincy Jones, David Byrne, and Arto Lindsay, bringing his distinctive sound to numerous recordings and live performances. Takuya Nakamura continues to push the boundaries of music, with recent projects blending his deep jazz roots with cutting-edge electronic production. His dedication to his craft and his ability to transcend genres make him a true pioneer

DISCO changed nightlife forever. But how did it all begin? What did Amsterdam sound like when the first disco records drifted in from New York? Who was there at the forefront when everything was still new, raw and exciting? And what remains of those nights filled with glitter, freedom and unapologetic dancing? During this ADE Arts & Culture special, we dive into the history of the disco scene and the dawn of the DJ era. From pioneers and tastemakers to clubs like Vrijhaven and today’s festivals. We trace the journey from disco to house and ask ourselves: is that energy still alive? Do we still dare to embrace the disco spirit? Expect stories, music, performances and fresh perspectives. We honour the past, question the present and celebrate everything in between.

descriptions.2815992: As if she’s sitting next to you on the couch, Diamanda La Berge Dramm’s voice is intimate and immediate. The simplicity of her speaking, singing and violin playing draws the listener into her fantasy world—magical and at the same time crystal clear. With simple tools—two violins, a small table, a studio lamp and a few pedals—she creates an intimate and crystal-clear world on stage. The audience witnesses the unfolding of Chimp’s sound world: the acoustic violin as the first source, the voice as transportation, and the electric violin facilitating it all. Nothing more than that—completely minimal. Yet the result is maximal. Drawing from her rich musical background, Dramm combines classical training, the American avant-garde, new music and a deep love of alternative pop. descriptions.2816040:
Uncompromising in form and driven by a rhythmic energy that defies all convention – that is Hoketus, the legendary composition by Louis Andriessen. Fifty years ago, Andriessen wrote this still-striking piece that reshaped the face of contemporary music. Hoketus became a cornerstone of the Dutch musical movement known as the Haagse School (The Hague School) and an enduring source of inspiration far beyond the Netherlands. Many composers have drawn from Andriessen’s propulsive rhythms, minimalist precision, and raw sonic world. For this anniversary celebration, Michael Gordon, co-founder of the legendary Bang on a Can collective, writes a mirror composition: a new work that confronts Hoketushead-on. Not a homage, but a next step in the path Andriessen set out – music that doesn’t yield, but clashes, moves, and breaks.

Thuishaven is not a club, or a warehouse. It’s a unique experience. Located on the Western outskirts of Amsterdam, the site is surrounded by heavy industry, massive oil tankers and scrap metal yards. Thuishaven has several stages, bars, surreal decoration pieces and curiosities. Incorporating materials purchased or found at neighboring scrap yards, the site radiates a raw and industrial atmosphere. During the winter set-up (October - April), all stages are housed indoor, in heated tents and a newly crafted hangar. The summer set-up (May - September) hosts a mesmerizing open air stage plus the option to use both tent and hangar for a raveyer vibe. With a track record of 200 festivals and counting, the site is ever evolving. Every new visit brings to light new details and new surprises—making it one of Amsterdam’s most extraordinary venues.

A monochromatic light instrument played through collective presence. White Space is an immersive installation that transforms negative space into a place where strangers connect.

At its heart, a monolith of intense blue and white light spins on its axis, casting compositions of monochromatic light and generative music that shift and dance among the audience. Responding to pose and position, the sculpture becomes an instrument, played by everyone present at once.

Only by coordinating their positions and synchronising their poses can visitors reach the climax of the installation: illuminating the emptiness that separates them and transforming the negative space into White Space.

In addition to the open deck session and exhibition, the film Funk (2026) will be screened on ADE Wednesday. Directed by Aly Muritiba, the film follows Sabrina, a young funk artist from the favelas of Rio de Janeiro, as she navigates the competitive baile funk scene. Set against a backdrop of heavy beats, bold performances, and the energy of the dance floor, the film explores themes of ambition, class, and the tension between commercial success and staying true to your roots. A post-film discussion with a guest speaker and actor in the movie Crazy Jeff will follow the screening. Like the rest of Studio/K’s ADE programme, Funk highlights baile funk not only as a music genre but as a cultural force that brings together community, creativity, and self-expression, connecting Brazil’s underground scene with contemporary club culture..

On 21 October, monumental music, art and architecture come together to celebrate 30 years of ADE. The Concertgebouworkest will perform Beethoven’s Fifth Symphony with 70 musicians inside Amsterdam’s monumental Centrale Markthal. Enjoy this true classic from 1808 conducted by Riccardo Minasi, beneath the largest-ever version of Boris Acket’s EINDER. The rhythmic motif of Beethoven’s Fifth Symphony is repeated constantly, taking on ever-changing forms, and in this way Beethoven builds his symphony layer by layer. While EINDER will shift and reshape above the orchestra creating a dance that is never the same twice. Beethoven’s Fifth Symphony was revolutionary 200 years ago, and it still is today. This energetic music never ceases to surprise. About EI

descriptions.2827839:
A full-body haptic and low-frequency music experience at The Stargate, bringing sound beyond the ears and into the body. Using cutting edge haptic mats, a group of participants will experience music through deep low-frequency vibrations and tactile sound, creating a physical dimension to listening. Bass becomes something to feel as much as hear, as vibration moves through the body in resonance with the music. Designed as a collective listening experience, the session explores the relationship between sound, vibration and physical sensation - inviting participants to experience music from an entirely different perspective. If you’ve ever found yourself standing in front of the speakers just to feel the bass, this one’s for you.

Initiated by artist Lawil Karama in conversation with historian Megan Hoetger, The Nature of Remembering is a group exhibition featuring multimedia research projects that move between interrogation of normative memory politics and co-experimentation with environmental and more-than-human bodies. The exhibition title carries in it two meanings: on the one hand, nature is evoked, drawing focus to actants, actors, and animacies beyond and beside the human, who witness, participate in, index, recollect, foretell, and haunt historical time. On the other hand, the idiomatic expression "the nature of" is taken up as a provocation, pushing against pervasive ideological and violently enforced notions of remembering and of commemorating.

Between 22-25 October, you can walk beneath the art installation EINDER by Boris Acket and experience it up close as it continuously transforms, flowing to the rhythm of day and night.

Ready to step into the art and leave time behind? During the EINDER exhibition, you decide how your experience unfolds and how long it lasts. descriptions.2829148:
Rooted in Culture returns to Stadsschouwburg Amsterdam (ITA) for it's fifth anniversary edition. This year's programme explores the journey of house music to Europe and the crucial role the UK played as its first European home. How did house find its roots in British street culture, sound system traditions and northern soul? And what did the UK bring back to the global sound? The evening features a dance workshop by an international guest from the UK house dance scene, an indepth session by resident cultural critic and DJ Lynnée Denise, and a closing jam session by DJ collective Chill on Tuesday.

Timetable: 12:30 doors open 13:00 - 14:30 workshop by Frankie J 15:00 - 16:30 In conversation with Lynnée Denise - UK Sounds influencing House culture 16:30 - 19:00 dancefloor session with Chill on Tuesday

descriptions.2829248: Live Coding Sessions and Doka Culture present an Algorave during Amsterdam Dance Event 2026. As the city welcomes the global electronic music community, we’re excited to celebrate the live coding scene alongside it. An Algorave (a combination of algorithm and rave) is a club night where music and visuals are created by writing code in real time. Rather than performing pre-recorded tracks, artists improvise throughout the night while their code is projected for the audience to follow, making the creative process part of the performance. We're thrilled to welcome a fantastic line-up of artists, with first-time Live Coding Sessions guests Hellocatfood, MYNA, Sol Sarratea, Deaxmachina and Den Ree, alongside returning favourites Jobi, Joyce den Hertog and Lil Bleep. descriptions.2829367: 99 years ago, Layla was filmed; the first Egyptian feature film. This marked the beginning of a film culture that became one of the shared languages ​​of the Arab world for decades. This exhibition, Dreams of Films – Films of Dreams, by Van Eesteren Museum and Moataz Rageb, brings back the visual world of cinema from that era. Here, you will discover original cinema posters, hand-painted billboards, and illustrated posters created by illustrators, calligraphers, and printers who are rarely known by name. In addition to images, sound and music also take center stage. Film music has always been inextricably linked to Egyptian cinema, and famous compositions were revived through another medium: on cassette tapes. He gained recognition through his sharp DJ sets and technically precise transitions, which collected millions of views online. At the same time, he built a distinct identity of his own, with support from the Soulection community and a steadily growing international fanbase. descriptions.2839353: This ADE, Herbavox and Techno Therapy are joining forces for a special Saturday afternoon session. Founded by Taylor Taylor, Herbavox has been throwing intimate, sub-100 capacity parties across Amsterdam since August 2024. Showcasing local talent, we keep things genre-fluid with a heavy emphasis on Electro-House and Electro-Funk, building a tight-knit community along the way. Techno Therapy, founded by Prabuddha, centers on dancefloor mindfulness and sustainable club culture—offering top-quality music that leaves you feeling uplifted rather than exhausted. Zone2Source presents an exhibition exploring electricity as a living network through works by Sunjoo Lee, Claire Williams and Ryan Jordan, in which technology, ecology and ritual become intertwined. Circuits and Ceremonies takes Sunjoo Lee’s long-term artistic research project Electric Garden as a starting point, a project initially developed in collaboration with FIBER. Zone2Source invited the artist to continue to explore the implications of her project further through engagement with the work of fellow artists who equally consider electricity not as an invisible, unlimited source of energy but as a living and relational process.

descriptions.2842428:
What happens when your eyes have nothing left to see? This short experiential performance by ArtEZ music theatre students takes place entirely in the dark. No set to look at, no face to read — only sound, voice, and space that you have to learn to trust.

The makers place themselves in a world without sight: which senses grow sharper, how does closeness feel without a gaze, does uncertainty make way for intimacy and intuition? A performance you don't watch, but undergo.

Four performances on ADE Friday at Theater de Richel. Very limited capacity for each performance.

Performance 1: 21:45 - 22:15 Performance 2: 22:30 - 23:00 Performance 3: 23:15 - 23:45 Performance 4: 00:00 - 00:30

Theater de Richel is an intimate theatre venue in a historic building in the heart of Amsterdam. Enjoy the programming in one of our three performance spaces and have a drink in one of our two cafés.

descriptions.2843071: This is not a regular concert. Come trip on the avant-garde sound world of Sofia Gubaidulina - the composer the Soviets tried to ban for being too radical - and the trance-ambient music of Soheil Shayesteh, live in one of Amsterdam's most beautiful hidden gems: the Uilenburgersjoel. Lay down. Let the sound move through the space and through you. There's no stage to face, no seat you're expected to sit still in - just a shifting, physical body of sound built to take you somewhere else, inside a 17th-century synagogue most of Amsterdam has never set foot in. The music itself moves in two directions at once. Gubaidulina's world is raw, confrontational, rooted in the physical - it pulls you down into the earth. Shayesteh's music reaches the other way, up toward something hypnotic and transcendent, closer to the heavens. Together they take you the whole way: from the earthly to the heavenly a

Club Up was born from a rather unusual piece of Amsterdam history. What started as a practical solution to an emergency exit requirement - eventually became a club of its own, tucked away behind Sociëteit De Kring, an artists’ society founded in 1922. Today, Club Up has its own identity, while remaining connected to the creative spirit and heritage of De Kring. The space is intimate, raw and deliberately a little hidden, with a focus on electronic clubnights with a creative and alternative spirit.

Ton Akkermans opens the portal with his hand-forged gongs, singing bowls, and chimes - instruments he crafts himself as a blacksmith, each one carrying its own voice. Fralalai weaves through the landscape with her harp and elven singing, carrying the listener deeper into the mist. Elizabeth Plokker (The Conscious Club) brings live field recordings from Glastonbury and ambient textures that root the journey in the natural world. Charon Tolhuisen guides the meditation, leading the way across the waters and into the heart of Avalon. A one-hour immersion in sound, story, and stillness. Facilitators: Charon Tolhuisen, Ton Akkermans, Elizabeth Plokker
descriptions.2844531: ADE - Cosmic Navigation ๑ Sound Journey & Guided Meditation To Sardinia A guided sound journey and meditation to the sacred well of Santa Cristina in Sardinia - an ancient site of water worship, built over 3,000 years ago, where the sun aligns with the water during the equinoxes, and where, every 18.6 years, the moon reaches its highest point and its light passes perpendicularly through the tholos to reflect on the water below. Ton Akkermans sounds the depths with his hand-forged gongs, singing bowls, and chimes - each instrument born from fire and metal in his own forge. Fralalai carries the voice of the ancient island of her ancestors through her harp and enchanting song. Elizabeth Plokker layers live field recordings from the well and ambient soundscapes that evoke the water, the stone, and the silence of the well. “What if creating a more accessible, safer, and inclusive nightlife isn’t about adding more rules — but about changing how we show up in the space?" Giulio Beja and Veronica Motta are ’Spazi Sensibili’, a project that explores accessibility, safety, and inclusivity within club and night culture as practices of collective care. Together, we will question who gets to feel safe, visible, heard, and free on the dancefloor — and who is still being excluded.

Through hands-on exercises, collective mapping, real-life nightlife scenarios, and open discussion, we will explore how discrimination and exclusion can show up in night spaces, while reflecting on our own experiences, perspectives, and capacity to intervene.

Mudcell Composition IV is a sound performance in collaboration with the microbial life of “Electric Garden”. Inspired by the longterm research project by Sunjoo Lee, Niels Gräber and Isaac van den Aker have developed a system to co-create sound with electrogenic bacteria, normally found in wetland mud. The organisms fluctuating voltages actively shaping the composition, influencing rhythms and frequencies.

The sound performance is part of the exhibition "Circuit and Ceremonies" by Sunjoo Lee, Claire Williams and Ryan Jordan at Zone2Source. The event will feature two performances at 11:15AM and at 12:15AM. There will be the opportunity to visit the exhibition and talk to the performers about their work.

Zone2Source is located in Amstelpark. The closest access is the so-called Red Bridge.

A monochromatic light instrument played through collective presence.

White Space is an immersive installation that transforms negative space into a place where strangers connect. At its heart, a monolith of intense blue and white light spins on its axis, casting compositions of monochromatic light and generative music that shift and dance among the audience. Responding to pose and position, the sculpture becomes an instrument, played by everyone present at once. Only by coordinating their positions and synchronising their poses can visitors reach the climax of the installation: illuminating the emptiness that separates them and transforming the negative space into White Space. White Space is an interactive light installation by artist Matthias Oostrik, who leads its concept, software, and production. During ADE, artist Sammie Tjon Sien Foek, also known as DJ Slimfit, will perform three shows featuring a hybrid live set at the historic clandestine church of Museum Ons' Lieve Heer op Solder. For this special curation, Slimfit explores the ritualesque quality of sound throughout differing historical and cultural contexts. By integrating and remixing classical music elements with live electronic composition influenced by ancestral rhythms, they reinterpret supposedly opposing liturgical ideologies.

Slimfit's practice centers on critical postcolonial theory and its friction with contemporary meaning-making within a metamodernist zeitgeist.

Futures of Listening comes to Amsterdam Dance Event 2026 with Currents, a four-day programme of experiments and performances in spatial sound at Loods6, from 22 to 25 October. Across three evenings of live and DJ sets, a day of workshops and demos, and a closing spatial sound meetup, artists will work with changing sound system configurations to shape a different listening experience each night. descriptions.2848944:

Alongside three evenings of live and DJ sets, the programme includes two days of hands-on workshops and demos and a closing spatial sound meetup, bringing together artists, makers and the wider community around the tools and techniques of spatial sound.

During Saturday afternoon, we’ll offer everyone who’s active as a DJ or live performer the chance to get to know Ambrio’s new spatial mixer. There will be a demonstration, you’ll be able to try out the mixer yourself, and there will be discussions with the artists who work with it and the creators at Ambrio. More news about the programme, including a masterclass in spatial sound, will follow very soon.

Presented by FIBER Festival, 4DSOUND, Ambrio, and CTM Festival
descriptions.2848981:
Gathering Sounds closes the Currents programme with a shift in register: from performance to practice, from audience to community. This is a day where the room turns inward, practitioners sharing what they're working on, and why.

Across an afternoon at Loods6, spatial sound practitioners take turns bringing something from their practice into the room: a tool, a patch, a speaker build, a piece in progress, a field recording, a research question, a score. Nothing here needs to be finished. This is a space for work that's still finding its shape, presented as an invitation to think and listen together. Gathering Sounds is part of a series of community events running throughout the Futures of Listening project, built to create space for exchange and connection outside of formal presentation contexts. Free entry.

Presented by FIBER Festival and 4DSOUND as part of Futures of Listening.

In 1992 the Warehouse, originally a peanut factory, located in the industrial West of Amsterdam hosted some of the very first large scale party raves called Multigroove. These nights set a milestone in Amsterdam's music development and party scene. Almost 20 years later, the mystical location re-opened its doors after being closed in 1993. Still with the same intention: to bring music from its purest side. And dance until sunrise. Today the Warehouse is home to some of the city's most renowned party concepts such as Hyte, Welcome to the Future indoor festival, Reaktor and Luciano & friends. Elementenstraat 25, Amsterdam West

The church is famous for many reasons, including being the burial ground of world famous painter Rembrandt van Rijn, hosting the royal wedding of former-queen Beatrix and it's iconic tower.

Pantheon Amsterdam brings together contemporary art, heritage and spirituality in a unique exhibition at Museum Ons’ Lieve Heer op Solder. Eight artists are creating new altarpieces and celebrations centred on stories of faith, identity, exclusion and recognition. Pantheon Amsterdam demonstrates that these subjects are not merely historical phenomena, but contemporary themes that continue to give meaning to the lives of many people.

One of these art installations is ‘Opacity’ by Sammie Tjon Sien Foek, also known as DJ Slimfit. During ADE, Slimfit will give three intimate performances in the museum’s clandestine church. By integrating and remixing classical music elements with live electronic composition influenced by ancestral rhythms, they reinterpret supposedly opposing liturgical ideologies. More information about the performances at this page.

Club shapeshifter BAMBII takes over Parallel on October 22 for an ADE evening show. Based in Canada, BAMBII has made a name for herself by refusing to stay in one lane. Her sets jump between global club sounds, dancehall, bass and rave, connecting scenes, eras and geographies while keeping the dancefloor at their core. That same instinct runs through her own productions: lush, bass-heavy and futuristic, with dancehall and her Jamaican heritage as a constant thread. Across both, the club becomes a space for movement, freedom and belonging. Having taken her sound across Europe and Asia and shared stages with artists including Kelela, Mykki Blanco and BbyMutha, BAMBII lands at Parallel for ADE alongside Amsterdam’s Jarreau Vandal and London-based Tsunamy

descriptions.2859563:
For this special edition of Transitions X Obsession, Carista takes us through a special selection of 4 of her favourite DJ mixes. We talk about DJing, mixes and the art of DJing. After the listening session, Carista will play a DJ set.

Carista is a Surinamese-Dutch phenomenon. DJing is only one facet of CARISTA's sprawling talents. Radiating warmth and spirit in every space, she puts her audience first, slipping into their shoes and imagining the dancefloor from their perspective. This approach informs her playful cross-pollination of 4/4 techno, bass, broken beat, electro, EBM, trippy left turns, and so much more. Constantly reading the room with razor-sharp ears and eyes, CARISTA conjures up a special connection with her crowd and is unafraid to challenge herself along the way.

"Vira", in Portuguese, means to turn or transform something — a situation, a scenario — in a positive way. VIRA becomes the cultural link between Brazil and the Netherlands, pulsing with music, art, nightlife, and the vibrant energy of both countries.

During ADE Week, Studio/K will be transformed into a free public exhibition space where photography, film, and digital storytelling come together. A photography exhibition featuring images from São Paulo and Amsterdam highlights the connections between the two cities.

The program concludes with an indepth session on the 24th of October featuring members of Encosta and ONDA Collective, followed by "Beats & Bites," an informal networking event that brings together artists, musicians, creatives, visitors, and professionals from the Dutch and Brazilian creative sectors.

The exhibition is free to visit. Open Wed-Sat 16:00-22:00.

descriptions.2861261: With raw, hypnotic beats, exhilarating chants and heavy basses, Arsenal Mikebe has steadily been infiltrating the international avant-garde. The Ugandian percussion group has celebrated triumphs at festivals such as Dekmantel and BRDCST and platforms such as Boiler Room. At the heart of their sonic identity is a steel percussion system, custom-made by Ugandan sculptor Henry Segamwenge and inspired by the Roland TR-808 drum computer. It makes the band become a living drum machine that sounds at least as intense and dynamic as today’s electronic dance music. Arsenal Mikebe is part of the Nyege Nyege collective, based in the outskirts of Kampala. The group is comprised of master drummers Ssentongo Moses, Dratele Epiphany, and Luyambi Vicent de Paul. descriptions.2861423: Every person who walks into Charged becomes exactly that. A cloud of light gathers around you, pulled in by your presence, and moves when you move. Some people you meet in it carry the same charge as you, and so push each other's energy away. Others carry the opposite, and your clouds fold into each other before either of you has decided to merge. As magnetic poles repel, opposites attract. The work is about how we change each other's environment simply by being in it, positively or negatively, whether we mean to or not. Charging and discharging as a way of interacting between persons. The more people step in, the more chaotic it becomes. With only a few, it settles into something calm and connected. The visuals in Charged were built with TouchDesigner, while its eye uses an open-source AI vision model called YOLO, which has become the standard way for a machine to find people in a camer

Part of ADE Arts & Culture, co-curated with Amsterdam Light Festival.

Amsterdam-based Touki Delphine is a boundary-pushing collective of musicians, performers, and visual artists. They are making waves both nationally and internationally with monumental light and sound installations, built from recycled materials: taillights in FIREBIRD, turn signal relays in RELAY, wiring in TRANSMISSION, windshield washer fluid reservoirs and their pump motors in DRIFTING. Their latest work, SUPERDRUM, is constructed from second-hand drums, wooden branches, and car door lock mechanisms. Through their work, they create musical poetic encounters between humans and machines. Inspired by natural systems, the climate crisis and the idea of nature as a living whole, they imagine a future in which people, nature and technology collaborate rather than compete, and where waste can be transformed into something

After being cancelled during ADE 2025 due to the adverse weather conditions, Heliotrope by Heleen Blanken & Daniel de Bruin is back at the ADE Lab Village in Westerpark during the ADE week 2026.

Heliotrope is a kinetic installation inspired by the natural phenomenon in which plants orient their leaves and blossoms toward the sun. The work takes this principle as both a biological reference and a metaphor, exploring processes of energy reception, tropistic behaviour, the atomic movements inherent to living matter, and the pulsating rhythms embedded within the natural world. This idea is translated into a mirrored installation. The mechanically engineered installation moves its blades, diffusing light beams, and reflecting its surroundings in a chaotic and refracted image. It explores parallels between manufactured and organic movements and tries to liquefy the barriers. Heliotrope transf

descriptions.2861861:
Lately we've observed fewer dancers on the dancefloor, fewer dancers hired or planned as part of an event's programming, and audiences standing facing the DJ with their phones out. What happened to dancing all night long, connecting to the music and to each other? Have we lost the essence of clubbing?

This indepth session is organized in the context of The Better Move, a project supported by VibeLab. Its goal is to increase the employment of dance professionals in the nighttime economy, and integrate more movement-based, health-enhancing, and culturally rooted experiences into club programming.

This event is donation-based. Would you like to support our work? You can donate via the QR code on the day of the event.

Club Up was born from a rather unusual piece of Amsterdam history. What started as a practical solution to an emergency exit requirement - eventually became a club of its own, tucked away behind Sociëteit De Kring, an artists’ society founded in 1922. Today, Club Up has its own identity, while remaining connected to the creative spirit and heritage of De Kring. The space is intimate, raw and deliberately a little hidden, with a focus on electronic clubnights with a creative and alternative spirit.

descriptions.2865518:
presented by WhyNot, Stadsherstel, and ADE Arts & Culture.

15 dancers explore the state of nightlife, post-clubbing.

“Wonderful and devastating performance (…) Definitely the most impressive group work I saw in years.” Fransien van der Putt, dramaturg, theatre critic and author.

Elisa Zuppini choreographs a system in which human perception converges with other-than-human agencies. Fifteen dancers form a pulsing structure, extending toward and withdrawing from the audience’s perceptual field. Like chthonic waves, they generate a hybrid circuit of sensation. Within the insomniac framework of post-clubbing, the dancers explore the effects and aftereffects of hedonistic nightlife. They perform through a dissociative state of depersonalization, allowing them to resource from something other than conditioned subjectivity. By inhabiting liminal and viscous spaces, the dancers explore multipl
descriptions.2865524: HUBS is een gratis en toegankelijk programma van Common Culture tijdens ADE, waarin jongeren in Amsterdam-Zuidoost kennismaken met elektronische muziek, de evenementenindustrie en de creatieve sector. Tijdens de Hub ontdek je op een interactieve manier wat er allemaal komt kijken bij de wereld achter de muziek. Van het ontdekken van DJ-gear en het maken van je eigen muziek tot het leren over eventproductie, programmering en de verschillende rollen binnen de muziekindustrie. Daarnaast zijn er talks, workshops en activiteiten waarin je zelf aan de slag gaat, nieuwe skills ontdekt en kennismaakt met professionals uit de creatieve sector. Er is ook volop ruimte om andere jonge creatieven uit de buurt te ontmoeten en te netwerken. Je hoeft geen ervaring te hebben: de Hub is juist bedoeld om te ontdekken, te experimenteren en kennis te maken met de verschillende mogelijkheden binnen de muzieki

Having collected over 200 millions streams, and with a European tour culminating in a Jazz Cafe headline show, dublon is now bringing his sounds into the very clubs he’s been so inspired by.

Nectar, his debut EP, is his most refined work yet, collating atmospheric toplines from vocalists and collaborations with renowned musicians Nathan Haines and Tour-Maubourg. It’s a collection of songs that emphasises his mastery of pop, classical and jazz sounds.

So far dublon has preformed as a DJ, but this fall he brings great jazz-musicians for a Live tour around Europe to show a different side of the project.

It’s sexy, thrilling and thought-provoking!

Striptopia is a captivating two-hour show that challenges stigma and celebrates the art forms of pole dance, drag, stripping and performance. This reimagined strip club is built on the values of honesty, safety, inclusivity and joy. Striptopia brings you face to face with outspoken performers in a fully interactive experience, where tipping via the Striptopia App, cheering and making contact are encouraged. Here, strip-club culture becomes something to celebrate, reflect on and reappraise.

About Striptopia: This isn’t a strip club relocated; it’s strip culture turned inside out. Built on consent, inclusivity and performer autonomy, Striptopia is a space where respect and celebration go hand in hand. Performers own their stage and boundaries, while guests are invited to explore and let go responsibly.

People on Music is a multidisciplinary crew of friends with a shared love for house music, founded in Amsterdam. The crew - after growing too big for a living room- is best known for hosting intimate, non-commercial daytime events built around warm and uplifting sounds. No line-ups or timetables are announced. Instead, the focus is on promoting raw talent and refined record bags, while leaving room for spontaneity and a dance floor where it’s all about people and the music. Alongside its parties, the crew has hosted radio shows, released a mix series on SoundCloud and organized vinyl markets serving delicious food. This event has very limited capacity. Mr. Fox takes over the decks for four hours of all-vinyl, no-shortcut house music. This ADE, Basshall takes over Parallel for a special night: Bashall Presents: Kybba. Pioneer and creator of the Basshall Movement, Kybba has shaped a unique sound where Dancehall, Caribbean and Latin influences collide with the vibrant sounds of islands such as Martinique and Guadalupe. descriptions.2889665: A concert film screening at Koninklijk Theater Tuschinski. On ADE Thursday, M07 premieres SIGNAL: a new concert film shot after dark across northern Vietnam. Across eight original tracks, hardware-driven electronics, processed vocals, custom instrument design and choreographed movement collide in a performance exploring the tension between technological overload and human stillness. The film was produced by Antiantiart, the Hanoi-based multidisciplinary collective behind Apple’s innovative 360-degree “Shot on iPhone” campaign. Co-founder Phuong Vu led the creative direction, with Hoang Dang, Hai Tom and Pham Duy directing. SIGNAL unfolds across northern Vietnam, with performances staged inside an abandoned circus on an island in Ha Long Bay and the concrete shell of an apartment block near Hanoi, transformed by a monumental LED screen spanning four storeys. Presented as part of the Amsterdam Museum's 100th anniversary, with the support of ADE Arts & Culture and Podiumkunst.net

For decades, Amsterdam's club culture has been a breeding ground for art, music, and social movements. From the legendary venues of the 1980s to today's nightlife scene, these are stories that have shaped the city. Yet this heritage is largely absent from official archives and collections. How do we ensure that the history of Amsterdam's nightlife is preserved, and for whom? Two art installations by MRLYN and State OFFF form an archive for night and club culture in their own way. The exhibition explores what it means to collect club culture: which objects, stories, and experiences deserve a place in archives and collections? Who are the custodians of this heritage, and what role can a city museum play in that? And how do you give a culture that is inherently fleeting

The wild nightlife of a New York club promoter is turned completely upside down when his 10-year-old son, whose existence he knew nothing about, suddenly appears in his life. Director and protagonist Jordan Firstman made a big impression this spring with Club Kid at the Cannes Film Festival. The film features top model Cara Delevingne, Colleen Camp, Kirby Howell-Baptiste and up-and-coming talent Reggie Absolom.

CLUB KID is a film by A24 and will be released in cinemas from 5 November. It will preview during ADE at Melkweg, ahead of the Dutch premiere.

descriptions.2892824: An evening program organized in collaboration with the ADE Arts & Culture program and Podiumkunst.net, presented as part of the Amsterdam Museum's 100th anniversary: a special program on collecting club culture. For decades, Amsterdam's club culture has been a breeding ground for art, music, and social movements. From the legendary venues of the 1980s to today's nightlife scene, these are stories that have shaped the city. Yet this heritage is largely absent from official archives and collections. How do we ensure that the history of Amsterdam's nightlife is preserved, and for whom? Especially for ADE, we present two art installations that each form an archive for night and club culture in their own way. Moving between Faces of Society, Chaos and Order, Empty Spaces, and The Solitude and the Self, the work looks beyond the obvious spectacle of nightlife. Close-ups, abstract details, fleeting encounters, and quiet spaces

On ADE Wednesday - whether lying down or sitting up - embark on a musical journey through time. A musical story that begins in Jamaica, with music by artists such as Donna Summer, Grandmaster Flash, and Kraftwerk, and - via Frankie Knuckles and Juan Atkins - passes through Chicago and Detroit before finally ending in Europe, and thus also in Amsterdam. The evening will feature hosts and DJs Nathan Kofi and Derk Louwes. The event will be conducted in English. For this unique event, only the seats next to the stage and a limited number of spots to lie down on the stage itself will be sold. This means the stage is rotated 180 degrees compared to the normal setup at The Concertgebouw's Main Hall.

Listening without distractions Through carefully selected tracks, sound fragments, and stories, Nathan Kofi and Derk Louwes make audible musical connections that you might not have noticed before:

The Node North will be hosting an free exposition with nightlife related art by Britta Moller from Wednesday October 20 till Sunday October 25.

Britta Möller is an Amsterdam-based artist creating large-scale abstract paintings wth acrylic, mixed media and layered textures. Her work explores transformation, surrender, visibility and concealment — themes rooted in the moment her former professional world came to a sudden stop during the pandemic. Before turning to painting, Möller worked for more than twenty-five years as a graphic designer and art director. In 1998, she co-founded Maslow, an Amsterdam-based design agency working for a wide range of organisations within the cultural sector. Maslow was responsible for the art direction and visual identity of Amsterdam Dance Event from 1998 to 2020, one of the key projects that shaped Möller’s strong position within the music and nightlife

In this new documentary, we immerse ourselves in the mysterious world of one of the most iconic clubs in the world – and accompany very different people through their Berlin nights. We meet Tim, alias Raven Van Krueger, who wants to make it big as a drag artist. Elisa discovers a new sexuality with her friends, a BDSM couple loves publicly, a dog play duo lives stability and excess, David tries to fight his way out of addiction. And club founder Simon seems out of step with the times – like many who once laid the foundations of the legendary KitKatClub.

Performances, discussions about consent, tender conversations with fathers, encounters between bodies and souls. "KitKatClub: Kinks of Berlin" is a cinematic experience about freedom, intimacy, identity, sex, and unlearning shame—raw and poetic at the same time.

Lauren Martin, the Scottish, London-based music writer and editor (formerly of RBMA, DJ Mag, and others), published "Aftershock: The Seismic Impact of Dubstep" in 2026 through Velocity Press. The first book on dubstep history, it's an oral history of the British electronic music genre’s origin story, as told through extensive interviews with 28 key artists and industry figures, and exclusive photography and visual ephemera from artists and photographers. For STILL DANCING, the photographer brings together more than a decade of this archive, from 2013 to the present photographed across Malta and the Netherlands. Moving between Faces of Society, Chaos and Order, Empty Spaces, and The Solitude and the Self, the work looks beyond the obvious spectacle of nightlife. Close-ups, abstract details, fleeting encounters, and quiet spaces

Delays, glitches, and interruptions that once made collective music-making almost impossible became the structure of the work. Live act transforming the signals from living fungi into sound

He has guided thousands of people through breathwork, live music, retreats and transformative experiences. For Mushroom Pulses, Kasper brings this background into a live audiovisual experiment centred around a living mushroom grow box - and treats the mushroom as another musician to jam with. descriptions.2903826: THE GREEN ROOM x ANOTHER RADIO- ADE 2026 Special Tijdens ADE brengt de stad vijf dagen lang de elektronische muziekscene samen. The Green Room zet de camera op wat daaráchter zit: de mensen, ideeën en keuzes die de cultuur maken, verder dan line-ups, releases en aankondigingen.The Green Room is een video-podcast over de cultuur achter elektronische muziek. Voor deze ADE-special strijkt het format neer bij Another Room, slow-fashion concept store en atelier in het centrum van Amsterdam, in samenwerking met Another Radio. In zestig minuten voelt het als een avond uit, met redactionele diepte: een cold open en scene-update zetten de toon, een persoonlijk hoofdgesprek met een gast vormt de kern, aangevuld met muziekverhalen uit Digging the Crates, en een field report en live session geven de aflevering een tastbaar slot.Het thema van deze editie: 30 jaar cultuur vooruit, legacy × next genera
descriptions.2903948: Van clubnachten tot ambient evenementen overdag, klub krai is geïnteresseerd in het experimenteren met luisterervaringen op het gebied van experimentele elektronische muziek, door zowel locale als internationale artiesten een podium te bieden. Naast de muziekprogrammering is er bij klub krai altijd een grote rol voor de ruimtelijke en visuele ervaring binnen een evenement, door middel van scenografische interventies wordt nagedacht over de fysieke ervaring van de dansvloer, maar ook de ruimtes op de randen van de dansvloer.Knaagfest is een nieuw evenement van Pixelateddunnehaarinsectencrazynesscollective. Knaagfest is een maximalistische clubavond die hyperpop, experimentele EDM en knaagdieren viert. descriptions.2904616: During ADE, the Allard Pierson brings Gaudeamus’s collection of contemporary composed music out of the archive and to life in a unique live setting. Producer and dj Tala Drum Corps (real name Tijmen Lohmeijer) and Georgian electronic producer Anushka Chkheidze present two adventurous live sets inspired by this remarkable musical source material. The Gaudeamus collection The Gaudeamus collection at the Allard Pierson contains contemporary composed music from 1945 to the present day. Alongside works by well-known composers, it holds a wealth of music by lesser-known artists from around the world. From sheet music and LPs to CDs, audio tapes and cassettes, the collection reveals how composers have been experimenting with sound, technology and new forms of music for decades. Step out of the noise of ADE and into a 75-minute journey back into your body.

This restorative session combines somatic practices, guided hypnotherapy, meditation and sound to help you slow down, settle your nervous system and reconnect with yourself. Move out of your head and into your body, creating space to notice what you need and let go of some of the tension you’ve been carrying. Through gentle somatic exploration and hypnotherapy, you’ll be invited to reset, reconnect and access a deeper sense of calm. Expect: * Somatic practices to reconnect with your body * Guided hypnotherapy & subconscious exploration * Nervous system regulation & deep relaxation * Singing bowls & meditation * Space to slow down, reset and reconnect with yourself

descriptions.2904664:
A 30-minute guided stretching session designed to release tension and restore mobility through the spine.

Moving through gentle, accessible stretches and controlled mobility exercises, the session focuses on creating more mobility through the spine, shoulders and hips while bringing awareness back to posture and movement. An ideal reset for a body that has been on the move, helping you loosen up, reconnect and feel more open for the rest of the day. Expect: • Gentle spinal stretches • Mobility-focused movement • Shoulder and hip opening • Breath-led movement • A focus on posture, range of motion and body awareness

descriptions.2904735:
Etherealism During ADE, Ethereal Africans presents a one-day cultural programme at Another Room with East African art, music and creativity at its centre. A stage for emerging and established East African artists & friends, DJs and performers, and an invitation to discover the diversity and coming together into the East African creative scene. Ethereal Africans grew out of something small, a group chat, started a year ago by a handful of East Africans in Amsterdam who rarely came across each other in the city. Its founders carry stories of migration and flight, and of growing up between cultures. What they built together is a place where none of that needs explaining. Gatherings where people share stories, poetry and music, and where, as they put it, you don't have to do it alone.

descriptions.2904857: In Berlin, you stop at the Späti for a beer on your way to the club. Four hours later you're still standing there, and it was one of the best nights you've ever had. Amsterdam has the same corner shops and none of the habit. Here, everything is booked weeks ahead. You barely meet anyone by accident. That's why Amsterdam Cornering Society exists. Free gatherings in and around avondwinkels. Standing at the corner. Letting things happen. You know the feeling if you've been in one at half past midnight. Fluorescent light. The hum of the fridges. Someone buying bread, someone buying a lighter, someone who just wanted somewhere to be. This ADE cornering edition happens at Avondwinkel van Wou, Van Woustraat 243. Orbit Wax is an independent record shop for underground electronic music, and it lives inside a Sense of Place. Percy runs it. He picks the records, he prices them, and on Sundays he plays them.

On the last day of ADE he plays from the shelves, noon until six. What comes out of the crates: Japanese psychedelics from the 80s and 90s, dub techno, minimal, ambient, downtempo, 2000s tech house. The thread through all of it, in his words, is "an endless, dreamy, hypnotic sound". The day starts easy, builds through the afternoon and settles again towards six.

Through the day he invites our resident selectors to the decks with him: the people who play the room on other Sundays of the year.

Most of the records you hear are in the shop, a few metres from the turntable. Listen first, then take one home.

Free entry, no reservation. Seated. Coffee is served as on any Sunday.

A respectful, positive proposal to share a moment together. Nothing imposed, only energy, consent and collective emotion. A powerful, emotional, dance-driven journey across Tech-House, House and Techno, curated and performed by Mosimann: a high-impact live DJ performance with strong crowd interaction, in a Boiler Room format that places the DJ in the heart of the crowd, not above it. Club Up was born from a rather unusual piece of Amsterdam history. What started as a practical solution to an emergency exit requirement - eventually became a club of its own, tucked away behind Sociëteit De Kring, an artists’ society founded in 1922. Today, Club Up has its own identity, while remaining connected to the creative spirit and heritage of De Kring. The space is intimate, raw and deliberately a little hidden, with a focus on electronic clubnights with a creative and alternative spirit.

descriptions.2916710: We start our ADE three-day performance program with Working (Título) | Cuddles are not enough, I need to be under your nails, sharing space with the dirt of your labor by Eloy Cruz del Prado. The performance points to a desire for intimacy that involves tenderness but goes beyond it. Through the sound of a waltz, a dance associated with coupling, but here danced with a hammer, and the words of James Baldwin’s Giovanni’s Room, in which desire, shame, and precarious living conditions are inseparable, the work treats affection and waged labor as entangled. The work asks how the material conditions in which we work and live shape the ways we love and care for others. What does intimacy look like when exhaustion and economic pressure are part of the relationship? descriptions.2917389:
Melting Image is a quiet resistance to how we consume images today — against the passive, one-dimensional scroll of the digital screen, it asks for presence instead of speed. Here, looking takes time, and the image only reveals itself to those willing to give it. An image is silkscreened onto layers of transparent material, then heat-formed until it lifts off the flat surface and takes on an organic, sculptural shape. Displayed in the gallery window, it turns the glass into a screen between street and space. Lit from behind by a slowly shifting projection, each layer catches the colour differently: parts of the image surface, others fade, never quite settling into one form. The longer you look, the more it keeps changing. Romina Koopman is a visual artist working at the edge of the tangible and the virtual, questioning how the digital image reshapes our perception of reality.

Melting Image is a quiet resistance to how we consume images today — against the passive, one-dimensional scroll of the digital screen, it asks for presence instead of speed. Here, looking takes time, and the image only reveals itself to those willing to give it. An image is silkscreened onto layers of transparent material, then heat-formed until it lifts off the flat surface and takes on an organic, sculptural shape. Displayed in the gallery window, it turns the glass into a screen between street and space. Lit from behind by a slowly shifting projection, each layer catches the colour differently: parts of the image surface, others fade, never quite settling into one form. The longer you look, the more it keeps changing. Romina Koopman is a visual artist working at the edge of the tangible and the virtual, questioning how the digital image reshapes our perception of reality.

descriptions.2918617: On the second evening of the ADE Arts & Culture programme, ROZENSTRAAT presents Sidario (2025-26) by Peruvian artist Wynnie Mynerva. Blood and a white shroud are the central materials of Mynerva’s performance, which is inspired by Loco afán: Crónicas de sidario (1996) by Chilean writer and performer Pedro Lemebel. In this work, Lemebel describes the lives and mortality of gay and trans people during the AIDS crisis. In Sidario, HIV is addressed not only as a medical condition, but also as a social and political issue. Mynerva brings together HIV, sex work, gender, racialisation and death with the exclusion and neglect experienced by certain bodies. Buh, a term used within trans communities in Peru to refer to HIV, appears as a virus that enters the exhibition space from the street and, as it were, ‘infects’ it. The session opens with sound transmissions from the Museum of Consciousness, followed by a talk by Carl Hayden Smith exploring how sound can transform perception, attention and our experience of reality. How does sound shape consciousness, and how might emerging technologies extend our capacity to listen, feel and perceive? Drawing on immersive artistic practice, psychoacoustics and archaeoacoustics, Smith explores the relationship between sound, embodiment, memory and altered states of consciousness. Moving between ancient acoustic traditions, contemporary technologies and scientific enquiry, the session examines the therapeutic potential of sound and asks a fundamental question: Can extraordinary listening experiences produce lasting changes in how we perceive, feel and act?

descriptions.2928552: RECUT Recut is an Italian Dj, producer and founder of Recut Music, with more than three decades deeply connected to vinyl and underground club culture. He started making music in the ’90s, coming from DMC culture and developing his approach through the art of storytelling with records. His sets are built around groove, strong musical roots and carefully selected records, moving naturally between Disco, Chicago House, Acid, Funk, Latin and other forms of electronic music. His musical philosophy is deeply influenced by the pioneers who shaped modern club culture and the art of Djing. descriptions.2929145: On the final evening of our ADE performance programme, we show Eclipse by Erik Tlaseca. In the performance, we encounter two characters: a child and a vampire. These apparent opposites both long for connection, understanding and care. The vampire becomes a figure for the desire for those fleeting moments of pleasure and intimacy that remind us that we are alive, precisely in a world where certain bodies and lives risk becoming invisible. The eclipse is the starting point for the work. In colonial Mexico, the phenomenon was represented by Indigenous artists as the moment when the sun closes its eyes; the sun did not disappear, but rather we disappeared from its sight. From this perspective, Tlaseca asks to what extent our memories remain present, and whether we can return to them. In loving memory of Jelmar van Belle, who filmed these videos during the closing of De School and sadly passed away on 20 February 2026. In January 2024, the renowned Amsterdam nightclub De School closed its doors. For more than eight years, it offered the city a unique space where everyone could truly be themselves. Behind these doors, a world of expression, love, fashion, and identity emerged. Clubs like this are more than nightlife venues, they are breeding grounds for culture.

The culture that forms around Amsterdam’s underground nightlife is shaped by people who cannot easily be defined. They often remain invisible to the outside world, partly due to the strict no-picture policy. Yet they are the ones who embody the color, creativity, and authenticity of the city. descriptions.2933806:
S!RENE is a Dutch DJ and producer with Nigerian roots. His playing style moves between global club, Afro influences, Hip-Hop, Funk, Jungle, R&B and electronic music, yet always feels cohesive.

He gained recognition through his sharp DJ sets and technically precise transitions, which collected millions of views online. At the same time, he built a distinct identity of his own, with support from the Soulection community and a steadily growing international fanbase.

As a DJ, he’s known for sets that build patiently before hitting hard. descriptions.2938577:
RUMBLE ADE SHOWCASE- Official ticket link

2 DJs. 1 Ring. Trading Bangers, Not Blows! The official RUMBLE debut at ADE 2026. Two DJs, face to face in the RUMBLE ring. Strictly no sync. You make the RUMBLE. Our own crowd tech, built just for this, measures the room's reaction live. Every scream, jump and hands-in-the-air moment feeds the show. The louder you go, the bigger the RUMBLE. It's never been done before, and you'll be in the room when it happens.

descriptions.2938666: BTDF is BACK with the original gang – for a special ADE edition. And we’re opening this new season with one idea: YOU are the main character of your life. Beyond The Dance Floor is an interactive social experience where we bring people together to connect and explore. In the middle of one of Amsterdam’s biggest weeks for music and nightlife, we’re creating a few hours to meet for meaningful & fun conversations, playful interactions, performances, movements and electronic music Áquila Allucard and Madina Flow reunite to direct the evening. Maybe it’s time to follow the script. Maybe it’s time to flip it completely. The atmosphere is curated by Jamal Erbilir. Live sound curation + DJ set by an artist from Amsterdam’s techno scene – announced soon. DRESS CODE: MAIN CHARACTER / MOVIE STAR Be creative. descriptions.2938767: THE OTHER SIDE nestled amidst Amsterdam's historic Houthavens embodies artistic evolution, creativity, and self-expression. Our club is among the select venues globally that boast revolutionary L-ISA immersive sound technology from L-Acoustics. The main room, with a capacity to accommodate 900 enthusiasts, is equipped with a state-of-the-art 14.1.5 L-Acoustics sound system that surrounds the audience, offering listeners unparalleled clarity, a natural auditory experience, and an expansive sound panorama. Doeshka Vrede and Jasper Lowik, the visionaries behind The Other Side, envisioned a space beyond just music. With L-ISA, this venue will not only amplify sound. Their sanctuary nurtures artists and visitors, aligning with nature's rhythms, inviting everyone to resonate with their authentic selves. descriptions.2938957: MINDGAME Records celebrates its 5-year anniversary on the water during ADE 2026 with an exclusive showcase in collaboration with Techno & Chill and Boatriders. On Thursday, October 22nd, Birds of Mind's label and Techno & Chill take over Eivissa for a cruise like no other – bringing together friends of the label and some of the artists who have been part of its journey for a special night during ADE. For the occasion, MINDGAME brings together an all-star lineup: Birds of Mind, AMÉMÉ, Moojo, Mont Rouge, Meloko, Baron, Amour Propre, KWEN, Kashovski, IMEN and Konvex. The celebration marks five years of MINDGAME – five years of releasing music from some of the scene's most exciting artists, gathering millions of streams, earning support from leading names across electronic music, and hosting showcases across Paris, Ibiza, Mykonos, Dubai and beyond. descriptions.2938963: Mixx Sound Network presents its Industry Mixer & Showcase - a premier gathering of global electronic music professionals during Amsterdam Dance Event. Celebrating ADE’s monumental 30th Anniversary, the Canadian network brings its signature energy to the heart of the city, taking over Club Prime on October 25th. Expect a carefully curated 4-hour sonic journey through Tech House, Melodic Techno, and Techno, featuring key artists from the Mixx Sound roster: MATT LUCKER, YIAO, JENNIFER SU and LAREINA LIU. About Mixx Sound Network: Mixx Sound Network is a pioneering 360-degree electronic music ecosystem based in Toronto. descriptions.2939227: CRANE HOTEL FARALDA ***** One of the most unique hotel experiences in the world you can find. Crane Hotel Faralda is one of the Secret hot spots in Amsterdam. The Crane is a 50 meters high monumental building. Two panorama elevators provide access right into the 3 design suites, the studio and the spa pool on top deck. Crane Hotel Faralda is situated on the banks of the river IJ and directly opposite the centre of Amsterdam. The view from each space is phenomenal. According to international press, Crane Hotel Faralda is one of the most romantic and inspiring places to stay. "Crane Hotel Faralda, for Creative and Passionate Free Spirits…." From 2011 it took 6 years to restore and redevelop this former piece of crap into 5 star hotel. The crane development has been a multimillion- devouring project. descriptions.2939289:
Two collectives. One shared love for house music. For the first time, Club Hacienda and STRAAL are joining forces, bringing together two communities from the South of the Netherlands for a special daytime session during Amsterdam Dance Event. On Sunday, October 25, the Venlo-based Club Hacienda and Roermond-based STRAAL take over DB55 for nine hours of house music. Expect a line-up that brings together both collectives’ sounds, familiar faces, fresh energy and a few surprises along the way.

Welcome to DB55, a versatile space for events and meetings, located in the heart of Amsterdam's Houthavens. DB55 blends hospitality with adaptable workspaces, entertainment, a collaborative community, and a vibrant social hub.

descriptions.2939376:
MADE is coming to Amsterdam to celebrate 30 years of Amsterdam Dance Event. Join us on Friday 23 October 2026, from 3pm to 7pm, at Ganbei Cocktail Bar for a free afternoon of good music and networking. With performances from some of the names making headlines in the UK: Connor Doonan, Corey Bell, Fletcher Kerr, Gemma Baxter, Joe Wilson, Laura Colandrea, Louis Johnstone, Roman Briggs, Usif and Zander. Alongside the DJ showcase, we will record a live podcast with guest interviews. There will also be plenty of time to meet people from across the music industry, connect with record labels and start new creative projects together. Whether you are a DJ, a producer, a label or simply in town for ADE, come and say hello. Free entry.

For the first time, Jângäl joins forces with London’s RECESS for a Sunday evening at The Hoxton, bringing two communities and two cities into the same room. We’ve followed what RECESS has been building in London for some time. There’s a shared understanding in how we approach nightlife: not simply as somewhere to go, but as a place where people, sounds and ideas can cross paths. Different cities, different communities, with enough common ground to make bringing them together feel natural. For our first edition together, we’ve invited a selection of artists from Amsterdam and London to take us through Sunday evening and into the final hours of ADE. Your favorite morning dance returns to ADE this year! Toast & Roast is teaming up with their friends at Amsterdam-Noord’s sickest venue: Het Dorp! Expect British heat from Mango & Ginger, bubbling legend Kaiena, and your usual local suspects, Yusu Selectors & Camtrao. Grab your tickets and get ready for some Sunday daytime raving!

Het Dorp is a cosy new venue in the North of Amsterdam, just one free ferry ride away from Amsterdam Central Station. With our homey atmosphere and views over the IJ, we are a place where people come together rather than a traditional club. Pick a drink, meet friends or strangers, have dinner, listen to music and dance! The programming at Het Dorp is intentionally varied and slightly unexpected.
